reports.title: Vipshop Reports Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Business Outlook
section: For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company expects its total net revenues to be between RMB29.2 billion and RMB30.9 billion, representing a year-over-year decrease of approximately 10% to 5%. These forecasts reflect the Company’s current and preliminary view on the market and operational conditions, which is subject to change.

desk.headline: Revenue down 4.3% to RMB20.4bn, in line; adjusted EPS per ADS of RMB2.64 missed; Q4 outlook of a 5–10% revenue decline
results: Revenue fell 4.3% to RMB20.4bn (US$3.0bn), at the low end of the company's range but slightly above the RMB20.40bn estimate.
Adjusted EPS per ADS fell to RMB2.64 from RMB2.98, below the RMB2.72 estimate; GAAP EPS per ADS was RMB2.21.
Active customers fell to 38.3m from 40.1m and orders to 151.8m from 166.4m, while gross margin held at 22.9%.
Lower admin costs lifted operating profit 3.8% to RMB1.31bn; Shan Shan Outlets GMV grew 11.7%.
Quarterly cash flow was negative (free cash outflow of RMB2.4bn); a special dividend of US$0.73 per ADS was declared and US$300m of shares have been bought back this year.

guidance.summary: For Q4 the company expects revenue of RMB29.2–30.9bn, a fall of about 5–10% from a year ago. It gives no profit guidance.

points: CEO Eric Shen called October sales "really bad", with only a limited recovery in November.
Management blamed cautious spending, holiday timing and unseasonal weather; a warm winter is expected to hurt clothing sales.
Super VIP members grew 9% and passed 10 million, making up 55% of online spending; a new tier system will reward bigger spenders.
The company said it avoided heavy subsidies despite promotional pressure, and is using AI for personalisation, service and marketing.
Total 2026 shareholder returns are put at about US$938m, including the upcoming special dividend.

watch: Whether the 8 December anniversary sale pulls Q4 revenue towards the top of the range.
Active customer numbers, which fell again this quarter.
Cash flow after a negative Q3, given the large dividends and buybacks.
